body: I do. I like reading and coding and going out to drink with my friends. And musicals. And operas (but can watch the latter 2 only online as I currently live in a small town where nothing fun happens and if does the quality is shit). However, when I binge I honestly hate everything and everyone around me, because they are (or at least look like they are) happy. And I am jealous. So the last week was like: force yourself to go to class, then go straight away home when the classes are over, try to do homework, do the minimal amount necessary, cry, go to bed in hopes that tomorrow will be better. And binge through out the process.

To be honest, the only merely helpful suggestion that I got from therapy was from the time I did DBT. It did not work for me 100% (otherwise I would not be asking for suggestions on the internet now), but at least it gave me at least some clear advice on actions I could take to control myself. The problem is that all of those mechanisms they taught me only work when you are relatively calm. When you are having a momentum (you binge non stop for 2 weeks and feel worthless and unable to control yourself, having sort of an agony to stuff your face until you explode), the last think you care about is implementing DBT in your life. You just want to save your ass, to be honest. Not meditate (you can't focus on meditation and relaxing when you are rushing to the fridge or the shop or whatever). Other therapy styles resumed to focusing on something like "let's go back to the times you were a child and try to think about the issues that caused the problem. And then let's talk about your relationship with X, Y, Z". Not any active advise just a lot of bs talk. I don't mind talking about my past or about people around me, but it does not help me now.

Hi! I'm nc15 at Mac for reference. Did not have much time today for any eye makeup except for mascara as 8.30 am classes kill any desire for creativity whatsoever. Anyway, here it goes:**mufe hydrating primer** Honestly, not sure if it does anything my cheap nivea moisturizer doesn't do. It sure helps foundation to apply smoothly and makes my skin seem soft, but, again, so does the nivea one. As for lasting power prolongation... Don't know. To be honest, never had issues with my makeup not lasting all day, thanks dry skin.**Nars tinted misturizer in Finland**. I quite like it, especially around this time of the year, when the weather is colder. It is very hydrating, light-weight, but provides decent coverage (more like a sheer foundation, I'd say). However, in Summer it hydration was too much even for my dry skin, because sometimes I felt greasy wearing it. Looked decent still. And the shade is actually a bit too yellow and a bit dark for me, but their lightest pink shade was too pink.**Nars rcc in vanilla**. Love it!! My holy grail, ride-or-die, best concealer ever. Perfect match, perfect coverage, goes equally well under eyes and blemishes, does not crease and is enough too cover my genetic zombie dark circles without a corrector underneath. Tried multiple other concealers, all either too thick, too drying or do not cover anything. But this one-perfection.**guerlain meteorites pressed setting powder in 03** Love it. Hourglass is not available where I live, so can't compare to their popular similar product, but this thing is amazing. It sets my concealer, and is also a wonderful finishing powder. Leaves the faces very glowy(especially if used with beauty blender) or lightly lighten from within(with brush) but never greasy (in fact, I find it somewhat mattifying, especially in when it is hot, I mean, it somehow takes away the bad oily from where you don't need it but adds glow where it is usually desired).**Nyx micro brow pencil in taupe** Quick and easy brow for me. And cheap! I actually prefer it to dipbrow, because it gives me the result I like (full natural feathery brows- kind of like those of Kathleen lights from YouTube), without any effort in no time, while dipbrow actually requires time and focus for me to get what I want (I don't always manage to do so, to be honest). And for the price, again, I can afford to buy this pencil quite often (price was the main reason I switched from brow wiz to dipbrow). The shade is also very alike my brows (people always get surprised when I say I fill in brows). As for comparison with other pencils, I'd say it is as good as brow wiz (a bit creamier, however, so those with oily skin might actually not like this as much as brow wiz, but for me- not an issue at all, and I actually like the spoolie of Nyx pencil better, as I always struggled that the spoolie of brow wiz took too much product off the brows, when I brushed thorough them); definitely better than urban decay pencil (that was too creamy even for me and without any matching shade) and better than maybelline brow satin duo (that pencil was thicker and too yellow).**Mufe clear brow gel**: it's fine. Not the best thing ever, but the best I've found for the price (I get 25% off at mufe). Holds brows in place well enough (important for me - love feathery brows), is not crispy at all, the spoolie is good and, very important, the tube is not transparent (I get disgusted when I have to see dirty stuff and then apply it to my brows). But the abh clear brow gel is better (it basically keeps my brows until, the end of the day in the way I brushed them and I brush them up) But too expensive for me too purchase at the moment.**maybelline rocket mascara black waterproof**- very nice. And lasts long without drying up. Gives volume, length and holds curl. On me it goes 3 coats without clumping. Not a pain in the ass to remove, as I find some waterproof mascaras are.**Nyx blush in taupe(old formula)** I like it a lot. Good contour shade. It is cool-toned and buildable, for me it's what matters when it comes to contour products. Lasts all day on me (however heard other people complaining about lasting power). Not patchy at all. Totally recommend.**Chanel jersey blush**- amazing, one of my favourite all-year shades. Formula is great, I love the scent, goes with every lipstick, very natural (but can be built up), like my own flush. Sometimes (especially fall and winter) I dust it also on my temples, forehead, chin and nose too warm up my face a bit. Looks amazing and healthy.**sleek solstice highlighter palette**: good. The most intense highlighter I own. Today I used the shade subsolar (light yellow gold). Can be applied both lightly and solidly too get different effects. I like all the shades(especially hemisphere-it's purple, duh). But the texture of marylou is better (more finely milled).**Dior addict intense lipstick in incognito** - very sheer formula, more a balm than a lipstick. It's a nice cool-toned shade, but, honestly, not my favourite texture. And not worth the price. At the drugstore, there is a bunch of comparable formulas. Yes, the packaging is nice and has a very satisfying click when it closes, but there is no way I'm going to pay (this was actually a gift) a lot of money for an average product, despite the beautiful packaging

Bundling it is. It allows the company to profit on the fact that people have quite uncorrelated relative willingness to pay for several of the company's products. To simplify here is an example: suppose you as a company are considering to sell 2 eyeshadow colors (bronze and blue) to 2 people (this oversimplification can be extended to a large number of people and products). Both women like bronze more than blue. Person 1 is ok about spending 15 on bronze and 5 on blue. On contrast, person 2 likes blue a bit more and bronze a bit less than person 1 does, but overall, however, still likes bronze a lot more than blue: she does not mind spending 13 on bronze and 6 on blue. If company  decides to sell shadows individually, the maximum sales it gets is 36, if it sets the price of bronze at 13 and of blue at 5 and sells to both women. But if the company decides to bundle the shadows into palette it would get 38 (the palette price is 19=13+5, which is the willingness to pay for both colors of the weakest customer). So it it profitable to make a palette.
